subject: conv-refusal-reason
text: - **Unreachable cause:** `viola_core::UnreachableCause` (`StrictModes` · `InstanceDead` · `UnwrappedName` · `EndpointLost` · `ServerVerify`, each word through `as_str`) is exit 21's closed cause set. It has no serde path: the two clients write every word. It is no `RefusalReason`.

subject: conv-exit-codes
text:
- **CLI exit codes:**
  - `0` ok
  - `1` internal error (anyhow edge), `viola run` refusing to start because its `ViolaName` is `live` or `stale` ([Session Liveness]; a live holder or a fresh replayed beat `detail:"already-live"`, stderr `unable: <name> is already live` / `hint: viola list`; a stale holder `detail:"stale-heartbeat"`, `unable: <name> is still running but not answering` with the stale hint), `viola run` refusing a pinned copy that fails its re-hash (`detail:"pinned-hash-mismatch"`, `unable: the pinned viola copy failed its integrity check`), `viola run` refusing a `.cmd`/`.bat` child program before any spawn (`process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"batch-script-child"}`, the two fixed `unable:`/`hint:` stderr lines), and `viola run` losing the exclusive endpoint bind to another holder (`detail:"squatted-name"`, `unable: the endpoint for <name> is held by another process` / `hint: another process holds this name's endpoint; stop it or pick another name`, no path, pid or pipe name); `viola revive` refusing its strict-modes check, which runs before the wrapper log opens and outside the preflight (`unable: <name>'s state files can be written by another user` and its `hint:` on stderr, exit 1, no log opened and no line written, on the start arm as on `--list`; chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor), and `viola revive` refusing at its preflight, whose four readings (the name's holder, the logged session, `session-live`, the recorded directory;
 chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board added the third) are taken in a fixed order and stop at the first refusal: `detail:"already-live"` or `detail:"stale-heartbeat"` (`run`'s own collision check and its two pairs, unchanged), `detail:"no-session"` (two pairs: `unable: <name> has no logged session to resume`, and `unable: <name> has no logged session with that id` for an `--id` the log does not hold), `detail:"session-live"` (`unable: <name>'s session is open in another claude` / `hint: close it there first, or start a copy: viola revive <name> --fork`, the founder's wording, his own answer to P4 fork 4 of chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board, `inputs#I1`; one `claude agents --json` read lists the logged id live in another `claude`; skipped under `--fork`; a failed read passes) and `detail:"cwd-missing"` (`unable: <name>'s recorded directory is missing`), each one `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr that holds no recorded directory, pid or logged id and one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail}` in `run-<name>.ndjson`; under `--json` each of these revive refusals, the strict-modes one included, and every refusal of the start it shares with `run` is instead one stdout document `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` (`strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing` · `stale-heartbeat` · `batch-script-child` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `internal-error`; `client::refused_document`) with stderr empty, the same exit 1 and the same log lines (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract), and a `pump_child` error, the child having held the terminal, prints none (`viola revive --list` has two refusals: the strict-modes check, the stderr pair or its document and exit 1 with no log line, and `no-session`, the stderr pair or its document and exit 1 with, under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`, `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"no-session"}` in the caller's `cli-<VIOLA_NAME>.ndjson`);
 `viola verify` with a failing ledger row (its stamp still written, last stdout line `stamped <ver>  <n> pass  <m> fail`), `viola verify` stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM before its rows are checked (no stamp written, stdout empty, stderr exactly `unable: verify was stopped before it finished` / `hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI`, and `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"interrupted"}` when `VIOLA_NAME` holds a valid name; chunk 2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup) and verify's refusals, each an `unable:` + `hint:` pair on stderr with no path: `the claude CLI was not found` / `install Claude Code or put it on PATH`, `the claude CLI is a .cmd or .bat script` / `pass the real executable, not a .cmd or .bat shim`, `the CLI version could not be read` / `run claude --version to check the install`, `a recorded fixture is not clean: <file> <code>` (a screen: `<file> row <n>[ seam] <code>`; codes `home-path` · `absolute-path` · `username` · `email`; never the content) / `record with a viola home under your user home`, plus run's pinned-copy re-hash refusal; and the `cli` role's internal error: `src/main.rs` `role_of` files every first word but `run`, `revive`, `mcp`, `hook` and a leading `-` flag under `cli` (a first word `mcp`, after any `--home <dir>` / `--home=<dir>`, is `Role::Mcp`, whose exit maps like `Other` and which never prints `error: internal error` — `prints_internal_error` stays `Cli`-only; chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers), and `revive` followed (after any `--home` pair) by `--list` before a `--` under `cli` too (every other `revive` is a wrapper beside `run`, and its start arm logs as process `run`; a `--list` after `--` is the child's word;
 so `send`, `wait`, `last`, `list`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`, `verify`, `revive --list` and `plugin install`), and a dispatch `Err` or a caught panic in any of them prints exactly `error: internal error` on stderr once, from the `main` catch site, no hint — no dispatch arm prints it; under `--json` before a `--` the catch site prints `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout in that line's place, stderr then empty; for `viola wait` / `viola last` exit 1 also covers a refusal reply, a reply of no known shape, and any channel error but a failed connect or a closed / reset connection (those are exit 21); for `viola link` / `viola unlink` exit 1 also covers a refusal reply and an `ok` of another shape than the verb's (`link`: a string `since` and a boolean `already_linked`; `unlink`: an object); for `viola list` exit 1 covers an `instances/` that exists and cannot be listed (or an entry whose type cannot be read) and a log start that fails, while a per-instance read error gives no row (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list)
  - `2` usage error (clap, a second positional to `viola send` included; never produced by `viola hook`), and `viola send` text over `MAX_FRAME` or not UTF-8 (`error: the text must be readable UTF-8 of at most 16 MiB`)
  - `10` `human-typing`
  - `11` `budget-paused`
  - `12` `unverified-cli`
  - `13` `not-delivered`
  - `14` `unknown` refusal
  - `20` protocol fault from the wrapper, a `-32602` from `link` / `unlink` included (a missing, non-string or invalid name, a `driven` that is not the serving wrapper's own name, or a `driver` equal to `driven`: the self-pair is refused by the wrapper only, never client-side)
  - `21` instance unreachable (no live endpoint for the `ViolaName`); also `viola list`'s refused strict-modes check of the home, `instances/` or any one instance, which refuses the whole board (`--json` `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}`, no log opened) — the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer (the operator's answer at chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list's planning, superseded 2026-10-13); `viola plugin install`'s refused strict-modes check of the home or an existing `marketplace/` tree dir is the same exit and document (human mode the home-state pair; nothing created, no log opened); `viola link` / `viola unlink`'s refused instance check of the driven instance (`check_instance` on the home and `instances/<driven>`, before any role file or log opens) is the same exit and document (human mode the instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair; no log opened, no line written, the mode left as found): exit 21 as for `list` and `plugin install`, not `revive`'s exit 1

subject: conv-exit-codes
text: - An absence: the socket-directory refusal has no code; `bind_endpoint`'s `create_private_dir` failure is an anyhow error at the catch site. OPEN — the socket-directory refusal's code · owner: the route entry "Unix endpoint and home hardening".

subject: conv-exit-codes
text: - Exit `21` also covers, on `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link` and `unlink`, a server that is not the recorded wrapper (the connected peer's pid or OS start time is not the snapshot's, or the check cannot be made): no frame is written, and the verb prints `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"server-verify-failed"}` under `--json` with stderr empty, or the `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` line with the server-verify hint last on stderr (its wording: design-system, surface cli-send). The client's own refusals (exit 13) and the strict-modes instance check (exit 21, `client::refuse_untrusted`: the target instance for `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release`, the driven instance for `link` / `unlink`) come first, before any connect, and the cause has no exit code or `RefusalReason` of its own, its `--json` word the document's `detail`.

subject: conv-exit-codes
text: - Exit `21`'s human hints: `src/human/hints.rs` holds the unwrapped-name hint and the endpoint-lost hint, each last on stderr and plain ASCII (their wording: design-system, surface cli-send). `src/cmd/client.rs` `hint_cause` keys the causes `not-running` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify`; `not-running` is the key of the cause the log reads `instance-dead`.

subject: conv-exit-codes
text: - An exception: `server-verify-failed` is claimed off macOS only; `v1-18`'s named carve-out leaves macOS's server check with the route entry "Unix endpoint and home hardening".

subject: conv-exit-codes
text: - Exit `21` also covers the refused strict-modes check of `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release` (`client::refuse_untrusted`: `check_instance` on the home and `instances/<name>`, the verb's first step, after its text read for `send`): human mode prints `link`'s instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, and `--json` exactly `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` with stderr empty; nothing under the home is opened and no line is written.

subject: conv-exit-codes
text: - Exit `21`'s CLI mapping: `src/cmd/client.rs` `answer_of` reads `Connect` as `Dead` and `Closed | Io` as `Lost`; the six no-endpoint arms (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `link`; `release` and `unlink` reach them through `wheel_call` and `link_call`) read `Unreachable::without_endpoint`.

subject: conv-mcp-results
text:
- **MCP:** a success is a tool result with `isError: false` and the channel `ok` payload as `structuredContent` (for `list`, the caller-side `{items, budget, skipped}` payload, the `list` payload of Standard Contracts). A refusal is a tool result with `isError: true` and the same `refusal` + `detail` in `structuredContent`. An unreachable instance and a wrapper protocol fault are also `isError: true` tool results. Their `structuredContent` is `{"error":"instance-unreachable"|"wrapper-fault","detail":…}`, the same as CLI `--json` (`instance-unreachable` with `detail` its cause word, `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed`; `wrapper-fault` with the JSON-RPC fault's `{code,message,data}` as `viola_channel::sanitised_fault` reads it: a fixed `message`, `data` a closed object or null). As landed (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers): each handler re-validates its raw argument object (`target` through `ViolaName::try_new`, `text` a string, `after` / `timeout_ms` absent, `null` or a `u64`, `dialog_id` a `u64`, `response` an object through `Response::parse`), and a failure is an `isError: true` result `{"error":"invalid-params","detail":"<field>"}` (the closed field words `target` · `text` · `after` · `timeout_ms` · `dialog_id` · `response`) with no frame written; every `isError` text is `refused: <code>`. JSON-RPC errors are the MCP connection's own faults, an unknown tool name (`-32602`) and an internal handler fault — any other channel error, a reply of no known shape, a `wait` / `last` refusal, a panicked call — which is `-32603` `internal error` with `data: null`. `tools/list`'s result carries `ttlMs` 0 and `cacheScope` `private`: claude 2.1.287 negotiates protocol `2026-07-28` and drops every tool of a list result without them (as measured live at that chunk, `evidence/live-mcp.md` start 1).
 claude 2.1.302 on that protocol opens with `server/discover` (its JSON-RPC id a string) and then `tools/list`, each carrying `_meta` (`io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion`, `…/clientInfo`, `…/clientCapabilities`), and sends no `initialize` or `notifications/initialized`; viola's two results each carry `ttlMs` 0 and `cacheScope` `private` (as measured live at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup-ii/evidence/live-tap.md`, start 2). That recorded exchange, `fixtures/claude/2.1.302/Mcp.tools-list-1.json`, is replayed against `viola mcp` by `tests/mcp_recorded_exchange.rs` (`viola-e2e`), which takes the `tools/list` response by its request's id and holds the served result to the recorded result's key and type shape, its tool names in order.

subject: conv-mcp-results
text: - A frame tool (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`) whose connected server is not the recorded wrapper (its pid or OS start time not the snapshot's, or the check cannot be made; the start time read on `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`) returns the `instance-unreachable` `isError` result, text `refused: instance-unreachable`, with no frame written and no log line.

subject: contract-channel-methods
text: - Before its first frame, the client of `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`, `hook.event` and `hook.dialog`, and of the MCP `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` tools, compares the connected stream's peer pid and that process's OS start time with the snapshot's `pid` and `started_at` from its one snapshot read (Session liveness, below); a mismatch, or a check that cannot be made, writes no frame. macOS reports no peer pid and stays a recorded gap.

subject: contract-channel-methods
text: - Before that comparison each client runs the instance's strict-modes check, and a refused check writes no frame and no line: `client::refuse_untrusted` for `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link` and `unlink`, the hook's `trusted` for `hook.event` and `hook.dialog`, and `strict::check_instance` in the MCP frame tools. Its one snapshot read is `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay`, and only a real snapshot goes on to the comparison.

subject: contract-channel-methods
text: - `hook.event`, sent id-less by `hook` once its instance check (`trusted`) and its server check have passed (a notification, no reply; a refused or absent instance, a replayed or absent snapshot or a failed server check sends nothing and the hook fails open): `{ts, event:{kind, data}}`. The wrapper re-validates the event (`kind` is one of the five hook kinds `session-start` · `prompt-submitted` · `turn-ended` · `session-end` · `activity`; `data` is an object; for `prompt-submitted`, `text` is a string and `origin` is `harness` · `human`) and appends `{v, ts:<append time>, instance, kind, source:"hook", data}` to `events.ndjson`. An invalid event is not appended, and an append failure is `-32603`. A `prompt-submitted` whose `text` exactly equals the in-flight `send`'s typed text (the sent text with every CR LF pair and every other CR as one LF, and without its trailing CR and LF characters; any `origin` the hook filed) is appended with `origin:"driver"` instead, and only then settles that send ([Delivery Confirmation]). The one in-flight send no `prompt-submitted` claims is a listed local command waiting for its post-condition: a `session-start` whose `cause` is `clear` and whose `agent_session_id` is a string differing from the remembered one is appended unchanged and only then settles it.

subject: contract-cli-json-output
text: - `viola link <driver> <driven> --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"since":…,"already_linked":…}}` (`since` a string, `already_linked` a boolean) and `viola unlink <driver> <driven> --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{}}`, each with exit 0. Their refused strict-modes check on the home and `instances/<driven>`, made before any role file or log opens, prints exactly `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` on stdout (exit 21), with stderr empty and no line in any log.

subject: contract-cli-json-output
text: - The exit-21 document's `detail` is one of five closed causes: `strict-modes-failed`, `instance-dead`, `unwrapped-name`, `endpoint-lost` and `server-verify-failed`; its `v` is 1 and its `error` `instance-unreachable` on all five.

subject: contract-cli-json-output
text: - `viola send`, `viola wait`, `viola last`, `viola answer`, `viola pause` and `viola release` print the same `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` on stdout under `--json` (exit 21) for their refused strict-modes check of the home and the target instance, made by `client::refuse_untrusted` before anything under the home is opened, with stderr empty and no line in any log.

subject: contract-cli-json-output
text: - `client::unreachable_document` is the one writer of the exit-21 CLI document; `refuse_untrusted` and `src/cmd/plugin.rs` write `StrictModes` through it, and `src/cmd/list.rs`'s `refused_document` builds `strict-modes-failed` as a `Value` for `board_document`, the board's only refusal.

subject: contract-cli-json-output
text: - `Launch` carries `json: bool` (`run` passes false, `revive` passes `args.json`). With it true, `refused_with` (`src/cmd/run.rs`) prints `refused_document` in place of the human pair for `batch-script-child`, `pinned-hash-mismatch` and `squatted-name`, and a program not found, which has no human pair, prints `internal-error`; each returns before `spawn_child`.
